extracted.intended_audience: students preparing the agrégation / advanced undergraduate or graduate mathematics students (ENS-style lectures)
extracted.subtask_description: A lecture/course syllabus and examiner guidance covering advanced undergraduate/graduate analysis topics (differentiability, inversion/implicit theorems, submanifolds, Taylor formulas, optimization, ODEs, numerical methods) aimed at candidates for the agrégation and ENS students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master and prove the local inversion theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to state, prove and apply the local inversion theorem (TIL) under the stated hypotheses (C1, Jacobian invertible); know examples and counterexamples demonstrating necessity of hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know versions replacing C1 by Ck and the holomorphic version; exercise 63 (in source) gives an example and a counterexample. Use in change of coordinates (e.g., polar). Be ready to present different proofs (including fixed-point reductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Master and prove the implicit function theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: State, prove and apply the implicit function theorem (TFI) including geometric interpretation and the relation to TIL (equivalence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle Ck and holomorphic variants; be aware of problematic points (e.g., where slope is infinite); show how φ inherits regularity of f and obtain Taylor expansions of the implicit function. Use examples like the circle; ex 78 and 84 referenced for applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be able to reduce inversion proofs to a fixed-point theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the technique of reducing local inversion/implicit proofs to a fixed-point theorem by recentering at 0 and constructing a contraction map φ(y,x) = y + x − f(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIL: reduce to 0 and apply Banach fixed-point (point fixe). Provide the TFI/TIL equivalence and use Picard-type arguments where helpful (see Cartan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove global inversion/diffeomorphism criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Show when a C1 map is a global diffeomorphism: compute Jacobian, show invertibility everywhere, prove injectivity (e.g., via mean-value inequalities), then show image is open and closed to deduce surjectivity onto Rn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: g(x,y) = (x + f(y), y + f(x)) with |f'| < 1 is a C1 diffeomorphism of R2 onto R2. Use global inversion theorem and show Imp(g) is open and closed and nonempty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain regularity transfer for implicit functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the implicit function φ has the same regularity class as f (e.g., if f is Ck then φ is Ck).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to derive Taylor expansions (DL) of φ when f is sufficiently smooth; refer to OA remark in notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inversion/implicit theorems in geometry (change of coordinates, exponential map)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply TIL/TFI to change of variables (polar coordinates) and to show the exponential map is a local diffeomorphism (but not necessarily global).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss limits of globality (e.g., exponential's image band |Im λ|) and examples like k-th root of a matrix or image of matrix exponential (Zavidovique).

rubrics_metrics.name: State and use the constant rank theorem, immersion and submersion facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Know definitions of immersion and submersion, existence of left inverses for immersions and right inverses for submersions, and the constant rank theorem consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in proofs that immersions/submersions produce local diffeomorphic behavior; apply to examples and tangent space descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define submanifolds of R^n and prove the submanifold theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Give precise definitions of smooth submanifolds (parametric and implicit), and prove the theorem characterizing submanifolds (using TIL/TFI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples (sphere, torus, graph of sin), and note which examples are not submanifolds (|x| graph, cusp y^2 = x^3, double point x^2 − y^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute and interpret tangent spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Define tangent vectors and tangent space; show tangent space equals kernel of Dg (implicit) or image of Dφ (parametric) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate with concrete examples (circle, ellipsoid), interpret geometrically and use in extrema linked interpretations. Emphasize affine-linear structure and dimension count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and apply Morse lemma and critical point signature
rubrics_metrics.description: State and apply the Morse lemma; use Hessian non-degeneracy to deduce local behavior and relate signature to type of extremum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to localization of surfaces relative to tangent planes, directions principal on quadrics, and extrema linked applications (e.g., relations to AM-GM). Include drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show that the set of matrices of given rank is a submanifold
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that {M in M_{n,p}(R) : rank M = r} is a submanifold of explicit dimension n^2 − (n − r)^2 (or per given formula) and give tangent space descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples: GL_n is open (dimension n^2), SL_n, SO_n, O_n are submanifolds of R^{n^2}; tangent at I_n is the Lie algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain measure-null sets on submanifolds and invariance under charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Define null (measure zero) subsets of a submanifold via charts and prove independence from choice of chart using Jacobian determinants (change of variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that if λ(ϕ(A)) = 0 then for other chart ψ, λ(ψ(A)) = 0 using Jacobian nonvanishing and change-of-variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be able to compute tangent plane equations concretely
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute tangent plane equations for surfaces in R^3 using different definitions (implicit/parametric/graph), and illustrate with drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit computations (e.g., circle, ellipsoid) and connect to Morse lemma and position of surface relative to tangent plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know differentiability basics and consequences (chain rule, uniqueness, partial derivatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: State definition and uniqueness of differential Df(a), chain rule, differentiability characterizations (C1 iff partials continuous), Jacobian properties and consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples and counterexamples; show bounded differential => Lipschitz, zero differential => function constant on connected components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master mean-value inequalities and their corollaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove inequalities of finite increments (Rolle, MVT in R^n variants) and use them (e.g., injectivity/inversion arguments, Lipschitzness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cartan's strong inequality on R^n is referenced. Apply to show injectivity in global inversion example and other consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the multiple Taylor formulas (Lagrange form, integral remainder, Taylor-Young)
rubrics_metrics.description: State and justify various Taylor formulas in one and several variables: equality of Taylor-Lagrange, integral remainder, Taylor-Young, uniqueness of limited development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jury warning: candidates should be able to justify remainder analysis and explain o and O notation. Be aware that existence of DL order two is not equivalent to second derivative existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Taylor expansions in geometry, asymptotics and numerical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Taylor formulas in geometry (local study of extrema), asymptotic methods (Laplace's method, stationary phase), and in numerical error estimates (Peano theorem for quadrature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know examples: Stirling via Laplace, method of Laplace/col, DSE and convergence of power series; be careful about hypotheses for remainder estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and apply optimization existence and uniqueness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: State conditions for existence (compactness/coercivity) and uniqueness (strict convexity) of minima; show strong convexity implies coercivity and unique minimizer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples: quadratic forms x ↦ ⟨Ax,x⟩, norms equivalence in finite dimension; know projection theorem in Hilbert spaces and Lax-Milgram/Stampacchia applications (Dirichlet problem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize extrema: first and second order optimality conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Give first-order critical point conditions and second-order Hessian-based conditions (including signature interpretations and counterexamples where Hessian test fails).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate second-order conditions to convexity; use examples x^2 − y^3, x^2 + y^4; state Morse lemma consequences when Hessian nondegenerate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat constrained optimization with Lagrange multipliers and admissible cones
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain Lagrange multipliers for equality-constrained problems, the cone of admissible directions and Euler-type inequalities for convex constraints; mention qualification conditions for inequality-constrained problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geometric interpretation and examples (AM-GM, extrema on ellipsoids), and indicate when constraint qualification is needed (notes say not done in detail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present and analyze numerical optimization methods (gradient/Newton/quasi-Newton)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and analyze descent methods: gradient (fixed/optimal step), Newton and quasi-Newton methods, secant in 1D; give convergence results (Kantorovich lemma etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orally emphasize that one does not invert Hessian directly in practice; discuss computational tradeoffs: Newton is fast but expensive; gradient is slower but memory-light; give proofs of convergence where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know Cauchy-Lipschitz (Picard-Lindelöf) theorem and solution maximality
rubrics_metrics.description: State and prove existence/uniqueness for ODEs under local/global Lipschitz hypotheses, define maximal/global solutions and the exit-from-compact principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include integral formulation and fixed-point proof on a 'cylinder of safety'; use Gronwall for uniqueness and to pass from local to global; give counterexamples (non-uniqueness like y' = 3|y|^{2/3}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Gronwall lemma and priori estimates for ODE analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Know and apply Gronwall inequality for uniqueness, globality proofs, and a priori bounds in ODE problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize its role in passing from local to global solutions and controlling growth (examples in notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Solve linear ODE systems via matrix exponentials and Wronskian formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive solution structure for linear systems (constant coefficients via exp(tA)), prove Wronskian/determinant formula, and handle variable coefficient cases using Duhamel/Raabe formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to explain why one can differentiate exp(tA) series termwise; show dimension of solution space and reduction of order using companion matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform qualitative analysis of autonomous systems and stability (Lyapunov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define autonomous systems, equilibria and stability types; state and apply Lyapunov theorems for linear and nonlinear systems and illustrate via phase portraits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples: small oscillations of pendulum, Van der Pol, Lotka-Volterra; present counterexamples related to Lyapunov assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study particular ODEs and special techniques (separation, Bernoulli, Riccati, periodic coeffs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve and analyze classes of ODEs: separable, Bernoulli, Riccati, linear periodic (Sturm theory), Hill/Mathieu equations and their qualitative behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide worked examples: RLC circuit, pendulum, Hill equation; discuss Floquet/Sturm periodic theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze numerical schemes for ODEs: consistency, stability, convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and apply notions of consistency, stability, convergence (Peano/Runge-Kutta examples), and discuss well-posedness and conditioning for numerical resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Euler, RK4, θ-scheme for heat equation as examples; stress local-Lipschitz conditions for convergence and cite Crouzeix-Mignot examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present rigorously with examples, drawings and counterexamples
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury expects clear presentations: rigorous statements and proofs, numerous instructive examples, well-chosen counterexamples, and many drawings (phase portraits, surfaces, charts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize concrete computations rather than excessive abstraction; include diagrams especially for geometry, phase portraits for ODEs, and error illustrations for numerical schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be able to explain notations and asymptotic symbols clearly (o and O)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be able to explain and justify uses of o(·) and O(·) notation in Taylor expansions and asymptotic estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jury worries about many candidates misusing or being unable to explain these notations; justify remainders in Taylor/Lagrange formulas carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish local vs global properties and present appropriate proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly separate local characterizations (e.g., Hessian test for local extremum) from global existence results (e.g., compactness/coercivity arguments), and use appropriate theorems for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide compactness arguments for existence, convexity arguments for uniqueness, and counterexamples showing local criteria may not imply global ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate optimization/ODE stability to spectral/linear algebra tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit spectral properties of matrices (e.g., positive-definiteness, exponentials) to analyze quadratic forms, least squares, stability of linear systems and link with functional analytic results (Lax-Milgram, projection theorem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure candidates can compute dimension of solution spaces, explain exponentials of matrices, and connect eigenstructure to dynamics and optimization.
